summary: Stone: a single stone picked up, rolled, thrown or set up, and stone as the stuff of walls, altars, tablets and idols. A stone could be a precious gem, a weight in the bag, a hailstone from heaven, or a likeness of what is hard, still and heavy, as a heart of stone or a body sinking “like a stone”. Scripture makes a stone the figure of Yahweh, “the stone of Israel”, and of his anointed: the stone the builders rejected, laid in Zion as a cornerstone, and in Daniel's Aramaic the stone cut out without hands that breaks the kingdoms of men and fills the earth. Every Semitic language but Arabic has the word: Akkadian abnu, Ugaritic and Phoenician ʾbn, Aramaic and Syriac ʾabnā, Ge'ez ʾəbn.

words.summary: About 270 times. Feminine (Gen 28:22 “this stone … will be”; 1Sa 17:49 “the stone sank”). The word for any stone, from a pebble in a sling to a great block of the temple; its uses spread out from the stone itself to what is made of it, what is measured by it, and what is like it.

senses.definition: A single stone or rock as it lies in the field or the water: picked up, slung, thrown, rolled, sat on or slept on.

evidence.note: Jacob “took of the stones of the place and put it at his head”.
The shepherds “roll the stone from the mouth of the well … and put the stone back on the mouth of the well”.
Moses' hands were heavy, “and they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it”.
David chose five smooth stones from the brook.
“He took from there a stone and slung it … and the stone sank into his forehead.”
“If a man strikes his neighbour with a stone or with his fist.”
“A stone of the hand by which one may die.”
Shimei threw stones at David.
“Waters wear away stones … so you destroy the hope of man.”
“A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones.”
“Build up the highway, clear it of stones.”
“Lest you strike your foot against a stone”; quoted at Mat 4:6.
“He who rolls a stone, it will come back on him.”
“They cut off my life in the pit and cast a stone on me.”

senses.definition: The stones with which the congregation put to death one condemned by the law, “stoned him with stone(s)” (רָגַם or סָקַל בָּאֶבֶן).

evidence.note: “The people of the land shall stone him with stone (יִרְגְּמֻהוּ בָאָבֶן).”
They brought out the one who cursed outside the camp “and stoned him with stone”.
“The man shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”
“All Israel stoned him with stone … and they stoned them with stones.”
Naboth, falsely accused, was stoned with stones.
Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned “in the court of the house of Yahweh”; named by Jesus at Mat 23:35.

senses.gloss: a stone set up as a pillar, witness or memorial
senses.definition: A stone set upright, or a heap of stones, to mark where God met his people or to stand as a witness to what was said and done.

evidence.note: Jacob set the stone up as a pillar and poured oil on it.
“This stone which I have set up as a pillar will be the house of God.”
Jacob and Laban's pillar and heap of stones, a witness between them.
“When your children ask, ‘What are these stones to you?’ … these stones shall be a memorial to the sons of Israel for ever.”
Twelve stones set up in the middle of the Jordan.
“This stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of Yahweh.”
Samuel set up a stone and called it אֶבֶן הָעָזֶר, “for hitherto Yahweh has helped us”.

senses.definition: Stone as the stuff things are made of: walls and houses, the temple's hewn blocks, altars, the tablets of the covenant, vessels.

evidence.note: At Babel “they had brick for stone, and bitumen for mortar”.
“Great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house, hewn stones.”
The house was built of “stone finished at the quarry”; no tool of iron was heard in it.
The diseased stones of a house taken out and replaced.
“If you make me an altar of stones, you shall not build it of hewn stone, for if you wield your tool on it you profane it.”
“Write on the stones all the words of this law very plainly.”
Elijah took twelve stones, by the number of the tribes, and built an altar.
“The tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment.”
“Two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.”
Blood “in vessels of wood and of stone”.

senses.definition: The stone that holds a building: laid at the corner or the foundation, or brought out as the last, the head of the work.

evidence.note: “The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner (לְרֹאשׁ פִּנָּה).”
“Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a founded foundation.”
“Who laid its cornerstone?”: the earth's.
“They shall not take from you a stone for a corner nor a stone for foundations.”
Zerubbabel “shall bring out the head stone (הָאֶבֶן הָרֹאשָׁה) with shoutings, ‘Grace, grace to it!’”

senses.definition: Stone shaped into gods: with wood, the stuff of idols that cannot see or hear, set against the living God.

evidence.note: “Gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.”
“They were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone.”
“Saying to a tree, ‘You are my father’, and to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’”
“To serve wood and stone.”
“Woe to him who says … to a silent stone, ‘Arise!’ … there is no breath at all in it.”

senses.definition: A gem: with a word for its kind or its worth (אֶבֶן יְקָרָה, אַבְנֵי שֹׁהַם), on the high priest's garments, in a crown, among a king's treasures.

evidence.note: “Two onyx stones (אַבְנֵי שֹׁהַם), and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.”
“Four rows of stone” in the breastpiece, each stone named.
“The stones were according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve.”
“Bdellium and the onyx stone are there.”
The crown of their king, “a talent of gold, and a precious stone (אֶבֶן יְקָרָה)”.
The queen of Sheba brought spices, gold and precious stone.
Zion's stones set in antimony, foundations of sapphires, gates of carbuncle, borders of “stones of delight”.
The king of Tyre (Ezk 28:12), covered with every precious stone.
“Like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne.”
“A bribe is a stone of favour in the eyes of its owner.”
“A land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you dig copper.”
“Iron is taken from dust, and stone is poured out as copper.”
The miner searches out “the stone of darkness and the shadow of death”.

senses.definition: A stone kept in the bag to weigh with; “stone and stone” is two sets of weights, one to buy with and one to sell.

evidence.note: “Just balances, just stones (אַבְנֵי צֶדֶק), a just ephah and a just hin.”
“You shall not have in your bag stone and stone, a great and a small.”
“All the stones of the bag are his work.”
“Stone and stone, ephah and ephah, both are an abomination to Yahweh.”
“A bag of deceitful stones.”
Absalom's hair weighed “two hundred shekels by the king's stone”.
“The stone of lead” on the mouth of the ephah.

senses.definition: The stone (or tin) weight on a builder's line.

evidence.note: “The line of chaos and the stones of emptiness” stretched over Edom: the builder's line and plummet used to unbuild.
“They shall see the stone, the tin, in the hand of Zerubbabel.”

senses.definition: Stones of ice that Yahweh casts down from heaven on his enemies (אֶבֶן בָּרָד, אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישׁ).

evidence.note: “Yahweh cast great stones from heaven on them … more died by the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword.”
“Cloudburst and tempest and hailstone.”
“You, great hailstones (אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישׁ), shall fall” on the whitewashed wall.
On Gog and his hordes: “flooding rain and great hailstones, fire and brimstone”.

senses.gloss: like stone: hard, still, heavy, sinking
senses.definition: In likenesses: what is hard, unfeeling, motionless, heavy, or sinks at once.

evidence.note: “They went down into the depths like a stone.”
“Their pursuers you threw into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.”
“By the greatness of your arm they are still as a stone (יִדְּמוּ כָּאָבֶן), till your people pass over.”
“His heart died within him, and he became a stone”: Nabal, struck motionless.
Leviathan's heart “cast like a stone”.
“Is my strength the strength of stones?”
“The waters hide themselves like stone”: frozen.
“Stone is heavy … but a fool's vexation is heavier than both.”
“I will take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh.”

senses.gloss: the stone: figure of Yahweh and his anointed
senses.definition: A stone as a title or figure: Yahweh “the stone of Israel”, a stone of stumbling to those who do not trust him, and the stone he lays and sets before his people, which the New Testament reads of Jesus Christ.

evidence.note: “From there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel (אֶבֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל)”, beside “the Mighty One of Jacob”.
Yahweh of hosts “shall be for a sanctuary, and for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both houses of Israel”; quoted at Rom 9:33 and 1Pe 2:8.
The stone laid in Zion; “he who trusts will not hasten”; quoted at Rom 9:33 and 1Pe 2:6.
Quoted by Jesus of himself (Mat 21:42) and by Peter (Act 4:11; 1Pe 2:7).
“The stone I have set before Joshua: on one stone seven eyes … and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.”
Jerusalem made “a stone of burden for all the peoples”: all who lift it are gashed.
“Did you never read in the scriptures, ‘The stone (λίθον) which the builders rejected…’”: Jesus of himself.
Christ the living stone, rejected by men but chosen by God; believers built on him as living stones. The Peshitta has ܐܒܢܐ at 2:8, its only use of the word, elsewhere ܟܐܦܐ.

evidence.locator: Gen.28.18, הָאֶבֶן → λίθον; Psa.118.22, אֶבֶן → λίθον; Isa.28.16, אֶבֶן → λίθον; Isa.8.14, אֶבֶן → λίθου; Psa.91.12, בָּאֶבֶן → λίθον

evidence.note: Quoting Psa 118:22.
Psa 118:22, with “everyone who falls on that stone will be broken, and on whomever it falls it will crush him”: the stumbling stone of Isa 8:14–15 and the falling stone of Dan 2:34, 44.
“This is the stone set at nought by you builders.”
Isa 28:16 and 8:14 joined: “I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling.”
Isa 28:16, Psa 118:22 and Isa 8:14 in turn.
Quoting Psa 91:12.

evidence.locator: Exo.31.18, אֶבֶן → λιθίνας; Ezk.11.19, הָאֶבֶן → λιθίνην; Ezk.36.26, הָאֶבֶן → λιθίνην

evidence.note: “Not on tablets of stone (πλαξὶν λιθίναις) but on tablets of hearts of flesh”: Exo 31:18 and Ezk 36:26 together.
Idols “of stone and of wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk”: the idols of Deu 4:28 and Dan 5:23.

parallels.note: Rock, paired with stone in the figure of Yahweh as stumbling block.

evidence.note: “A stone of stumbling and a rock (צוּר) of offence.”

parallels.note: Wood, the other stuff of idols, nearly always named with stone.

evidence.note: Vessels of wood and stone.

parallels.note: Iron, in the land whose stones are iron.

opposites.note: A heart of flesh, given in place of the heart of stone.
Brick, used at Babel in place of stone.

phrases.gloss: stone and stone: two sets of weights
stone with stone(s): put to death by stoning
Ebenezer, “the stone of the help”, a place

evidence.note: “Hitherto Yahweh has helped us.”

phrases.gloss: the stone of Bohan, a boundary mark
the stone of Zoheleth, by En-rogel
the stone Ezel, where David hid

words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, eight times, emphatic אַבְנָא: the stone of Nebuchadnezzar's dream, the stone on the mouth of the lions' den, the stone of idols, and the great stones of the rebuilt house of God.

senses.definition: A single stone: the stone laid on the mouth of the den, and the stone of the dream, cut out without hands, which struck the image and became a mountain.

evidence.note: “A stone (אֶבֶן חֲדָה) was brought and laid on the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet.”
“A stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.”
“The stone (אַבְנָא) that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.”
“A stone was cut out of the mountain not by hands … the great God has made known to the king what shall be after this.”

senses.definition: With gold, silver, bronze, iron and wood, the stuff of the gods Belshazzar praised.

evidence.note: “They praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.”
“Gods of … wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know; but the God in whose hand is your breath … you have not honoured.”

senses.definition: The great stones of the house of God at Jerusalem as it was rebuilt.

evidence.note: “The house of the great God … is being built with great stones (אֶבֶן גְּלָל), and timber is laid in the walls.”
“Three courses of great stones and a course of new timber.”

evidence.locator: Dan.2.34, אֶבֶן → λίθος; Dan.2.45, אֶבֶן → λίθον

evidence.note: “On whomever it falls, it will crush him (λικμήσει)”: the falling stone of Dan 2:34–35, which made the image like chaff.

words.gloss: (dual) a pair of stones: potter's wheel; birth-stones
words.summary: Only twice, both in the dual אָבְנַיִם, “the two stones”: the potter's wheel, and what the Hebrew women sat on to give birth. Both are things made of a pair of stones or discs, which ties the word to אֶבֶן; with only two uses, what the objects looked like rests on the word's form and its two contexts.

senses.definition: The pair of wheels or discs at which the potter works.

evidence.note: “I went down to the potter's house, and behold, he was doing work on the two stones (עַל־הָאָבְנָיִם).”

senses.definition: The pair of stones (or a stool) a woman sat on in giving birth, where the midwives saw the child.

evidence.note: “When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the two stones (עַל־הָאָבְנָיִם), if it is a son, kill him.”

cognates.gloss: stone; precious stone, jewel, bead; hailstone; kernel, pit; stone in the body
cognates.note: The same spread of senses as the Hebrew: a stone, a gem, and a hailstone.

evidence.note: “stone”; inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʾabn-.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the Targum renders Jacob's stone (Gen 28:18) and the onyx stones (Exo 28:11) by it, and it is used of weight-stones, as the Hebrew.

evidence.note: Targ. Gen. XXVIII, 18; pl. אַבְנַיָּא, Targ. Ex. XXVIII, 11; “א׳ דאכפא weight-stones”.

cognates.note: In the Peshitta New Testament only at 1Pe 2:8, “a stone of stumbling”, quoting Isa 8:14; its usual word for stone is ܟܐܦܐ.

evidence.note: “rock, stone (substance or piece); gem”.
“stone”; from Proto-Semitic *ʔabn-.

doctrine.statement: Nebuchadnezzar saw an image of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay, and “a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and broke them in pieces”; the metals became “like chaff of the summer threshing floors, and the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them; and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth” (Dan 2:34–35). Daniel explains: “in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed … it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever” (Dan 2:44–45). The stone does not grow among the kingdoms or change them; it strikes them all at once at the last, and only after they are gone does it fill the earth. Jesus took to himself the stone of Psa 118:22, “the stone which the builders rejected”, and added, “everyone who falls on that stone will be broken, and on whomever it falls, it will crush him” (Mat 21:42–44; Luk 20:17–18): the rejected stone of the psalm is the falling stone of Daniel. Peter names the builders, “this is the stone which was set at nought by you builders”, Jesus whom they crucified and God raised from the dead (Act 4:10–11), and Paul and Peter read Isa 28:16 and 8:14 of him, a foundation for those who trust and a stone of stumbling for those who do not (Rom 9:33; 1Pe 2:6–8). From the verses: the stone is the Christ, rejected and raised; the kingdom it brings is set up by God, not by the hands of men, on the earth, which it fills after the kingdoms of men have been destroyed, and it stands for ever.

The covenant at Sinai was written “on tablets of stone, written with the finger of God” (Exo 31:18; Deu 4:13). Through Ezekiel Yahweh promises the scattered house of Israel, “I will take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in my statutes” (Ezk 11:19–20), and again, with their return to the land, “a new heart I will give you and a new spirit … and I will put my spirit within you” (Ezk 36:26–27), as Jeremiah says he will write his law “on their heart” (Jer 31:33). Paul sets the two side by side: the believers are a letter of Christ “written not with ink but with the spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of hearts of flesh” (2Co 3:3). From the verses: a heart of stone is one that does not respond to God's word, and the change is God's work, by his spirit, writing his law where it moves a man to obey.

Moses warned that in exile Israel would serve “gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell” (Deu 4:28). Habakkuk mocks the man who says “to a silent stone, ‘Arise!’ … there is no breath at all in it” (Hab 2:19), and Jeremiah the people who say “to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me’” (Jer 2:27). Daniel told Belshazzar that he had praised “gods of … wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know”, but had not honoured “the God in whose hand is your breath” (Dan 5:23). Paul at Athens: “we ought not to think the Godhead is like gold or silver or stone, graven by art and man's device” (Act 17:29). From the verses: a stone god has no breath and no senses; the true God is the one who gives man his breath and holds it, so that a man's life is in his hand and not his own.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key אבנ; no existing entry used it. BDB keys: a.am.aa אֶבֶן (Hebrew), xa.ac.ac (BDB's Aramaic אֶבֶן; the corpus files most of its 66 tokens by spelling under Hebrew verses too, which the brief marks “also”; its own Aramaic tokens are Dan 2:34, 35, 45; 5:4, 23; 6:18; Ezr 5:8; 6:4, and Dan 2:34, 45; 6:18; Ezr 5:8; 6:4 are also counted under a.am.aa), a.am.ab אֹבֶן. No personal name is formed from the root: אַבְנֵר Abner is filed by BDB under אב (“father of light/Ner”) and is not taken here; Ebenezer, Eben-bohan, Zoheleth and Ezel are places, recorded as phrases. No merged letters (א ב נ), so no `sounds`. Arabic has no cognate for stone (it uses ḥajar); Lane's ءبن (p. 9–10: “impute”, “follow traces, eulogize the dead”, أُبْنَةٌ “a knot in wood”) shares no sense and is not recorded. Akkadian abnu was not checked in CAD; Ugaritic, Phoenician and Ge'ez rest on Wiktionary and Anderson–Moser only (DULAT/Segert, Krahmalkov, Dillmann not consulted). The brief found no New Testament quotations by alignment, though Psa 118:22, Isa 28:16, Isa 8:14 and Psa 91:12 are plainly quoted; they are added by hand. Peshitta: ܐܒܢܐ only at 1Pe 2:8 (SEDRA lexeme 17); the Peshitta's ordinary word for stone is ܟܐܦܐ. Septuagint στάθμιον (weights, Deu 25:13) and κατάλιθος are not recorded, being absent from the New Testament. Open questions: (1) אֹבֶן — whether it is a by-form or dual of אֶבֶן or a separate noun, and its gender; its kin to stone-material is by form and sense only. (2) Zec 3:9 and Zec 4:7, 10 are read under stone-figure, cornerstone and plummet respectively; whether the stone before Joshua is the Christ (cf. Zec 3:8 “my servant the Branch”) is for review. (3) The doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
